_doc: Headwaters source registry - Visakhapatnam (GVMC, Andhra Pradesh). Schema: scripts/check-upstream-editions.ts SourceEntry.

LICENCE POSTURE. Three postures sit in this scope. (1) We have not found a licence on APWRIMS or APPCB, and both sites print 'All Rights Reserved' in the footer, so they are carried as restricted even though the data is served openly. (2) Government of India and municipal publications (CGWB, MoHUA, NGT records, GVMC documents) are cited with attribution. (3) OpenStreetMap is ODbL share-alike.

ONE PORTAL, THREE FEEDS. APWRIMS (apwrims.ap.gov.in, Water Resources Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh) serves reservoir storage, groundwater sensors and the minor-irrigation tank layer through a public JSON API and WFS, with no login. Each feed is its own entry because each has its own cadence and its own failure modes (the groundwater archive carries values forward; the tank layer has no timestamp).

CLOSED AND REVIEWED DOCUMENTS. Every document a Vizag surface cites that is not a feed (government orders, audits, court orders, plans, registers, clearances, archival records and papers) has its own entry, from viwsco-project-pages on. A closed one carries cadence 'closed (...)' and a human review that only confirms the URL still serves it: every 365 days, or every 180 where a newer report or an amendment may follow (cag-polavaram-audit-2025, moefcc-ec-amns-anakapalli-2026). Each review is recorded in lastSeen (edition, acceptedOn, reviewedOn). Their postures: APSDMA and VIWSCO print a copyright footer and we have not found a licence, as for APWRIMS; the AP Government Orders Issue Register and the MoEFCC Wetlands of India portal allow reproduction with acknowledgement; INCOIS does not allow commercial reproduction, so it is linked only. Press reports are named as press where they appear and are not registered.

WHAT IS NOT HERE. The 98-ward boundaries are an Esri India tracing of a GVMC CAD plot, and we have not found a licence anywhere in the chain, and GVMC moved to 120 wards in 2026, for which we have not found public geometry; no ward artifact ships. Internal validation material from the owner is not cited.

sources.publisher: Water Resources Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh (APWRIMS)
sources.license: Andhra Pradesh Water Resources Department portal (APWRIMS): we have not found a licence or terms of use on the portal, only a disclaimer and a site footer reading 'All Rights Reserved' - Andhra Pradesh government data, cited with attribution
sources.notes: POST /api/reservoir/timeseries returns level (m), storage (TMC), inflow and outflow per reservoir per day, with no login. Daily archive near-complete for Yeleru from 2012 (short months in 2015-2017; Apr-Jun 2017 rows carry storage but no level). Raiwada is partial in 2012, has nothing in 2013, then runs from Oct 2014 (no usable values Nov 2015 to Jun 2016). Thatipudi runs from Oct 2014, Meghadrigedda from Nov 2015. GVMC's own Mudasarlova reservoir and the Water Resources Department's Gambhiramgedda reservoir are not in APWRIMS. Single-day requests for 2016-2019 return the next morning's reading under the requested key; range requests do not. Key on the IST date of levelStorageEventGenTS. The scraper checks each dam's design values (FRL, gross, dead storage) against reservoirAttrs on every run and exits 2 on a change. Certificate for apwrims.ap.gov.in expires 13 Dec 2026.

sources.publisher: Water Resources Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh (APWRIMS groundwater sensors)
sources.license: Andhra Pradesh Water Resources Department portal (APWRIMS): we have not found a licence or terms of use on the portal, only a disclaimer and a site footer reading 'All Rights Reserved' - Andhra Pradesh government data, cited with attribution
sources.notes: Two networks: the older APGW piezometers (mostly from Sep 2022) and the SENSOR_DATA network installed Dec 2025-Jan 2026. The archive endpoint carried one value forward for 195 days at Visalakshinagar and interpolates gaps of up to 30 days; one station id can carry different names in different endpoints. An unknown station id in the archive request silently returns every station in the state. The station producer also names each well by the mandal its coordinates fall in on the APWRIMS GeoServer mandal layer APWRIMS:AP_MANDAL_V3 (https://geo.vassarlabs.com/geoserver/APWRIMS/ows).

sources.publisher: Water Resources Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh (APWRIMS minor-irrigation tank layer)
sources.license: Andhra Pradesh Water Resources Department portal (APWRIMS): we have not found a licence or terms of use on the portal, only a disclaimer and a site footer reading 'All Rights Reserved' - Andhra Pradesh government data, cited with attribution
sources.notes: 38,443 tank polygons statewide; capacity carries no unit and the fill field has no timestamp, so only identity, name and location are used.

sources.publisher: IN-GRES (CGWB + Andhra Pradesh Ground Water and Water Audit Department), IIT Hyderabad
sources.license: no explicit licence: we have not found terms of use, a disclaimer or a copyright or licence statement on the IN-GRES portal; a Government of India assessment portal, cited with attribution
sources.notes: Assessed at mandal level. The 2024-2025 edition matches CGWB's 'Dynamic Ground Water Resources of Andhra Pradesh State 2025' (Dec 2025) for these mandals. TRAPS: the district id is reused across the April 2022 split (its district rows cover 8,547.7 km2 in 2016-2017 and 11,050.6 km2 in 2019-2020, then 1,001.7 km2, the assessed area of the new district, from 2021-2022) and the single 513.8 km2 GVMC unit became seven urban mandals in 2023-24, so no trend is quoted across either redraw. The 2025-2026 edition copies 2024-25 rainfall for every Vizag mandal and is newer than CGWB's December 2025 report. Use currentAvailabilityForAllPurposes (extractable): for Andhra Pradesh, totalGWAvailability adds the in-storage resource and is about 190 times larger. Unit polygons: GeoServer layer gec:indgec_mandal_all, year 2023, whose uuid is the assessment API's own. Detection: url-template POSTs the IN-GRES open API once per assessment year (recipe in ingres-gw-assessment-tn). lastSeen is the OLDEST edition any dependsOn file carries, so a partly refreshed scope keeps alerting.

sources.license: Government of India open data portal: its copyright policy permits reproduction free of charge in any format without specific permission, reproduced accurately and with the source prominently acknowledged; cited with attribution
sources.notes: Andhra Pradesh Ground Water Department manual MONTHLY resource 7df4b96d-3af5-4b16-b714-74ff6426ff5f runs 2002-05 to 2026-04 and is the long record behind the APWRIMS sensors; the station counts are in the stations file. The telemetry resources b57798f7-9a87-423f-9b99-c7d15eacc902 and 0e97a298-62b4-444c-81d6-599264010ebd are read only to check which APWRIMS recorder is which. sources.publisher: India Meteorological Department (0.25 degree gridded rainfall)
sources.license: IMD data policy; gridded rainfall retrieved programmatically via imdlib, cited with attribution
sources.notes: Grid cell 17.75 N 83.25 E, on land inside GVMC. Coastal trap: 17.5/83.0, 17.5/83.25 and 17.75/83.5 are ocean (all NaN every year), and a nearest-cell pick there writes zeros. Checked against IMD's Visakhapatnam airport observatory normal (station 43149, Climatological Table 1991-2020) of 1,054.5 mm: the cell's 1991-2020 mean is 1,053.4 mm. IMD's other Visakhapatnam observatory (station 43150) gives 1,113.1 mm and the AP planning department's district normal, cited in CGWB's 2025 aquifer plan, is 1,117.7 mm. The station tables are registered as imd-climatological-tables-visakhapatnam.

lastSeen.edition: IMD 0.25 degree grid, cell 17.75N 83.25E, years 1970-2025

sources.publisher: Central Pollution Control Board (National Water Quality Monitoring Programme)
sources.license: restrictive, permission required: the CPCB website policy permits material to be 'downloaded to file or printer without requiring specific prior permission', and 'Any other proposed use of the material is subject to the approval of competent authority of CPCB' - no redistribution without approval
sources.notes: CPCB's 2019-2024 tables have NO river-type station on any Vizag or Anakapalli river. The stations are coastal, one lake (Kondakarla Ava), one canal (Yeleru near Pharma City), two reservoirs (Meghadrigedda, Thatipudi) and a creek at the Naval Dockyard. TRAP: CPCB's 'Gostani' (4372/4373, and the polluted stretch) is in West Godavari at Vendra, not Vizag's Gosthani. 2024 split files must be read by word bounding box; plain text extraction attaches a neighbouring station's values. Also read for the facts: CPCB's polluted river stretch lists of September 2018, 2022 and October 2025 (the copy NMCG hosts). None of their Andhra Pradesh stretches is in Visakhapatnam; their 'Gostani' at Vendra is in West Godavari.

sources.refreshMethod: manual: read new affidavits in NGT OA 14/2021 (SZ), OA 40/2024 (SZ), OA 141/2023 (SZ), OA 130/2024 (SZ), OA 240/2025 (SZ) and NGT Principal Bench OA 606/2018 (AP compliance)
sources.notes: The only source-by-source supply table from GVMC itself that we have found is one day (11-03-2021), annexed to its action-taken report in NGT OA 14/2021 (SZ). Its net total is a fixed 0.85 of the gross (a flat 15% deduction), and its LPCD is the domestic share (net minus a 13.88 MGD industrial figure, itself 70% of the metered supply to industrial bulk consumers, with the Naval Dockyard and MES raw water counted at 90%) over an assumed 2.30 million people; both are derived, not measured. GVMC's 334.03 MLD 'present water supply' is from the Chief Secretary's report to the NGT Principal Bench in OA 606/2018, dated 10.07.2024 (Annexure-VI, PDF p33; https://www.greentribunal.gov.in/sites/default/files/news_updates/REPORT%20BY%20CS,%20GOVT.%20OF%20ANDHRA%20PRADESH%20IN%20OA%20NO.%20606%20of%202018%20COMPLIANCE%20OF%20MSW%20MANAGEMENT%20RULES,2016.pdf). Also read: the joint committee's report of April 2021 to the NGT Principal Bench in OA 175/2018, PDF pp4-5, on the Purushottapatnam lift (origins story), and the state's monthly progress report for February 2024 in NGT Principal Bench OA 673/2018, annexed to APPCB's report of 11.05.2024 in OA 40/2024 (SZ) (commitments register).
